title: Aamir Khan Denies 3 Idiots Character Was Inspired by Sonam Wangchuk
excerpt: Speaking at the London Indian Film Festival, the actor dismissed the long-held belief that Phunsukh Wangdu was modelled on the Ladakhi education reformer, calling it a 'misconception' and adding that co-star Omi Vaidya's claim was wrong.
body:
• Aamir Khan said neither he nor the makers of 3 Idiots knew about Sonam Wangchuk when the 2009 film was being developed.
  • He dismissed co-star Omi Vaidya's claim that the character Phunsukh Wangdu was inspired by Wangchuk, quipping: "Chatur is wrong."
  • The clarification came during a session at the London Indian Film Festival, where Lagaan was screened to celebrate its 25th anniversary.
  • Aamir expressed deep concern over Wangchuk's ongoing hunger strike at Delhi's Jantar Mantar and urged him to end his fast.

Actor Aamir Khan has categorically denied that the beloved character Phunsukh Wangdu — better known as Rancho — from the 2009 blockbuster 3 Idiots was inspired by Ladakhi education reformer and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk. The statement, made during an audience interaction at the 17th London Indian Film Festival on July 16, puts to rest over a decade of public speculation linking the two.

What Aamir Khan Said

The discussion arose at the British Film Institute following a special screening of Lagaan, which marked 25 years since the film's release. When a journalist raised the connection between Wangchuk and 3 Idiots, Aamir was unequivocal in his response.

"No, that is not true actually. That is a misconception. I didn't know about Mr Sonam at that time when we were doing the film. Neither Raju nor Abhijat — we didn't know about Mr Sonam."

— Aamir Khan, at the London Indian Film Festival

The actor was referring to director Rajkumar Hirani and screenwriter Abhijat Joshi, the creative team behind the film. He stressed that none of them were aware of Wangchuk or his educational work in Ladakh during the scripting and production process.

"The actor expressed genuine concern over the 58-year-old reformer's deteriorating health.</p> <p>"All of us are very concerned for his health and his life."

The 'Chatur Is Wrong' Moment

Aamir's remarks directly addressed a recent viral video by his 3 Idiots co-star Omi Vaidya, who played the character Chatur Ramalingam in the film. Vaidya had released an emotional appeal in support of Wangchuk's ongoing hunger strike and stated that the character of Phunsukh Wangdu was inspired by the activist's real-life work.

Disagreeing with his former co-star, Aamir said with a smile: "I saw a video of Chatur just recently, and he said that. But he is wrong. Maybe that is what Chatur was thinking." The quip — delivered in character — drew attention online, but Aamir was careful to separate the myth from the man.

"What Mr Sonam is doing is good work in any case. He doesn't have to be based on a character of 3 Idiots for us to respect him and the work that he does."

— Aamir Khan

The Origin of the Myth

The belief that Wangchuk inspired Rancho has circulated since the film's release in 2009. Wangchuk, an engineer who founded the Students' Educational and Cultural Movement of Ladakh (SECMOL) and pioneered innovative ice stupa technology for water conservation, seemed to mirror the film's protagonist — a free-thinking inventor who challenges the rote-learning system. The character's name, Phunsukh Wangdu, with its Ladakhi ring, cemented the association in public memory.

Wangchuk himself addressed this in a past interview with Hindustan Times, clarifying that the film was not a biopic and that the character bore little resemblance to his actual life. 3 Idiots was officially adapted from Chetan Bhagat's novel Five Point Someone, though the degree of creative departure has been a separate source of debate.

Concern Over Wangchuk's Hunger Strike

Beyond the film debate, Aamir used the forum to address Wangchuk's indefinite hunger strike at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, where the activist has been protesting over demands related to Ladakh's governance and environmental protections. The actor expressed genuine concern over the 58-year-old reformer's deteriorating health.

"All of us are very concerned for his health and his life. We hope it ends well. All of us are hoping that he ends his fast," Aamir said.

Wangchuk's protest has drawn support from several figures in the Indian film industry, including Abhay Deol, Swara Bhasker, Sonakshi Sinha, Prakash Raj, and filmmaker Anurag Kashyap.

Why It Matters for the Diaspora

For Indian audiences abroad, 3 Idiots remains a cultural touchstone — one of the most widely watched Hindi films in the global diaspora. The Rancho-Wangchuk narrative has been repeated in countless NRI WhatsApp groups, campus screenings, and social media posts for years. Aamir's clarification resets a piece of Bollywood lore that many took as fact, while simultaneously drawing international attention to Wangchuk's real and ongoing activism in Ladakh.
